problems.source_says: The paper explicitly reports random assignment of participants to three between-subject treatments, but does not establish the randomization unit. Table D.2 lists 2 HI sessions, 2 HAT sessions, and 5 HHT sessions; these sum to the 9 first-wave sessions reported in Section 2.3, implying one treatment per session. The PDF does not explain whether people were randomized into treatment-specific sessions or sessions were randomized after recruitment. Neither individual-level nor session-level allocation can be confirmed from this description. The form acknowledges this ambiguity in its notes, but still gives the categorical unit as individual.
problems.locator: PDF p. 19 (index 18), Appendix D, Table D.2, No. sessions row; column order Training, HAT, HI, HHT. See also p. 6 (index 5), Section 2.3, nine first-wave sessions; p. 2 (index 1), Section 1, random-assignment statement.

confirmed.statement: S1: The paper explicitly states, "In the first wave, 246 participants were recruited and randomly assigned to one of three between-subject treatments."
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 2, Section 1, paragraph beginning The experiment was implemented with two waves of experimental sessions.

confirmed.statement: S1: HAT participants received access to ChatGPT 3.5 while producing their own picture ideas in tasks 2 and 3; this is assistance to creators, not merely assignment of outputs to evaluators.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 2, Section 1; p. 4, Section 2.1 and Table 1; p. 5, Section 2.2.

confirmed.statement: S1: ChatGPT 3.5 was the generative language-model tool, accessed through poe.com for participant interaction.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 2.1; p. 6, Sections 2.2 and 2.3, especially footnote 7.

confirmed.statement: S1: The comparison arms match the form: HI worked alone without ChatGPT in tasks 2 and 3; HHT worked in anonymous human pairs with random rematching for each task and one joint submission.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Table 1 and Section 2.1; p. 6, Section 2.3.

confirmed.statement: S1: Reported arm sizes are HI 63, HAT 61, and HHT 122 people forming 61 teams; Appendix B.2 excludes one HAT participant from grade analyses, supporting the derived HAT analyzed count of 60.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 2.1; p. 17, Appendix B.2; p. 19, Table D.2.

confirmed.statement: S1: All three arms had the same 12-minute ChatGPT familiarization before an unassisted first task; the assistance contrast applies to tasks 2 and 3.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 2, Section 1; p. 4, Section 2.1 and Table 1.

confirmed.statement: S1: The two task themes were explicitly randomized in order, while treatment conditions remained between subjects across tasks 2 and 3; this is not a crossover requiring randomized AI/no-AI condition order.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 2, Section 1; p. 4, Table 1 and Section 2.1; p. 5, Section 2.2.

confirmed.statement: S1: Experimenters subsequently rendered submitted ideas with DALL-E 3 through ChatGPT-4o; text-only and text-plus-image evaluations do not replace the participant-level ChatGPT-access treatment contrast.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 2.2; p. 6, Section 2.2; p. 17, Appendix B.2.

confirmed.statement: S1: The authors report preregistering the design and intended analyses at AsPredicted.org; the preregistration and deviations are referred to an external supplement.

S2: Training recruited 56 additional participants in a later wave, and the main text warns about time and selection differences; Appendix B.2 inconsistently describes four randomized groups, a conflict already recorded in the form.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 1; p. 5, Section 2.1; p. 6, Section 2.3; p. 17, Appendix B.2.

confirmed.statement: S3: The standalone ChatGPT benchmark used experimenter-generated ideas, not another randomized assignment of people to assistance; the form correctly separates it.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 4.1; p. 20, Tables D.4 and D.5.

summary: S1 explicitly randomized participants to ChatGPT 3.5 assistance, unaided individual work, or human pairing, so criterion 1 holds. The individual assignment-unit code is unconfirmed because the PDF reports treatment-specific sessions without explaining the allocation procedure.
